title: AARC: Automated Affinity-aware Resource Configuration for Serverless Workflows
problem: Traditional serverless resource allocation couples CPU and memory, creating suboptimal provisioning for diverse workloads. Decoupling improves flexibility but introduces a massive configuration space that is difficult to optimize for complex workflows.
motivation: Serverless computing handles increasingly complex event-driven workloads, but inefficient resource provisioning leads to high costs and SLO violations. Decoupled resources offer flexibility but require intelligent configuration to avoid exponential search space.
method: AARC uses a Graph-Centric Scheduler to identify critical paths in workflow DAGs, then applies a Priority Configurator using priority scheduling techniques to optimize CPU-memory allocation. The approach reduces search time by focusing on high-impact configuration decisions and maintaining SLO compliance.
key_novelty: First automated framework for decoupled CPU-memory configuration in serverless workflows via graph-centric path identification and priority-based resource scheduling, achieving 85-89% search time reduction.
contributions: Graph-Centric Scheduler identifying critical paths in serverless workflow DAGs.
Priority Configurator applying priority scheduling to decouple CPU-memory optimization.
85.8-89.6% search time reduction and 49.6-61.7% cost savings while maintaining SLO compliance.
primary_theme: automated decoupled resource configuration for serverless workflows
